title: Flat scalar restriction and the normalized direct-image strict-limit square
statement:
Let $u:\mathscr U\to\mathscr V$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by small sites, meaning $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with finite-limit-preserving inverse image [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For $T=U,V$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings, with $S_T$ flat over $R_T$ (extension of scalars is exact). Fix isomorphisms $u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$, $u^{-1}S_V\cong S_U$ commuting with $a_T$. Use unbounded derived module categories, obtained by localizing cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived strict diagrams with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$ [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Write $r_T$ for restriction of scalars, on modules or diagrams [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $R_u^R,R_u^S$ for ambient derived direct image, and $\mathscr R_u^R,\mathscr R_u^S$ for derived termwise direct image. Let $\chi_u:r_VR_u^S\cong R_u^Rr_U$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^S\cong\mathscr R_u^Rr_U$ be exactly the flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]. Put $\mathcal L_T^R=R\lim$, $\mathcal L_T^S=R\lim$ on strict diagrams, computed by a K-injective tower resolution followed by ordinary inverse limit; K-injective means that every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Let $\kappa_u^R,\kappa_u^S$ denote the canonical direct-image/limit comparisons induced by $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^{J}$ [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison].

For every $Z\in D(\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_U)))$, and analogously at $V$, there is a natural isomorphism $\lambda_Z:r_U\mathcal L_U^SZ\cong\mathcal L_U^Rr_UZ$. Its specified ordinary comparison sends a compatible family to that same family, and its derived comparison on a K-injective tower is that ordinary comparison conjugated by the universal total-derived units. With these normalizations one has
$$\mathcal L_V^R(d_{u,Z})\lambda_{\mathscr R_u^SZ}\,r_V(\kappa_u^S(Z))=\kappa_u^R(r_UZ)R_u^R(\lambda_Z)\chi_{u,\mathcal L_U^SZ}.$$
This equality is natural in every derived strict tower $Z$, with no finite-reduction or completeness condition.

proof.text: Write $F_B=u_{*,B}$ and $F_B^J$ for ordinary direct image, $B=R,S$, and $Q$ for localization. For every strict $S_T$-tower $C$, construct $\rho_{T,C}:r_T\lim_{S_T}C\to\lim_{R_T}r_TC$ as follows. On each site object its map sends $(x_n)_n$ to $(x_n)_n$, with the $R_T$-action through $a_T$ on every component. Compatible families form a sheaf: matching families glue uniquely component by component, and the transition equations persist by uniqueness. The same formula in reverse is linear and commutes with restrictions, so $\rho$ is a natural isomorphism, also degreewise for complexes. With these sectionwise limit choices it is an identity. The flat diagram-restriction lemma gives exactness and K-injective preservation of $r_T$, for $J$ and for the one-object category, and the ordinary identity comparison $\delta_C:r_VF_S^JC\to F_R^Jr_UC$, including its analogue on single modules. We use those specified comparisons throughout.

source.place: Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules), Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); ordinary scalar comparison as specified in the cited flat diagram lemma

proof.text: All four tower module categories have enough K-injectives. Indeed the diagram-site realization identifies each with modules on a small ringed site; the ring sheaf is commutative because its sections are the given commutative ring sections. Apply the ringed-site K-injective existence theorem there and transport through the exact additive equivalence. This transport preserves acyclicity and the equation defining chain homotopy, hence preserves K-injectivity. Consequently every derived tower object is isomorphic to $QI$ for a K-injective tower complex $I$. The same existence assertion applies to the four module categories themselves. In particular the total derived functors under discussion exist and their universal units are invertible on K-injectives by the K-injective total-derived theorem; the specified strict derived limit is the K-injective computation in the strict-tower limit lemma.

Apply the K-injective exact-square comparison to $H'=\lim_{S_T}$, $H=\lim_{R_T}$, $r=r_T$ on towers and $s=r_T$ on modules. Its equality $sH'=Hr$ is the sectionwise equality of step 1; for other chosen limits use the unique identification $\rho$. Its exactness and K-injective-preservation assumptions are step 1, and enough K-injectives is step 2. This supplies a natural isomorphism $\lambda:r_T\mathcal L_T^S\to\mathcal L_T^Rr_T$, for both $T=U,V$. If $e^B_{T,I}:Q\lim_{B_T}I\to\mathcal L_T^B(QI)$ denotes the universal limit unit, its normalization is precisely
$$\lambda_{QI}\,r_T(e^S_{T,I})=e^R_{T,r_TI}\,Q(\rho_{T,I}).$$
Here and below the canonical exact-localization identifications are understood as in the cited comparison lemma. Thus this is the required normalization by universal units, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the endpoints.

source.place: Tags 070I, 070Y, 070K; existing exact-square comparison specialized to ordinary inverse limit

proof.text: The geometric inverse-image exactness lemma applies to $u$ on both ring sheaves. Since $u^{-1}B_V\cong B_U$, its transported module inverse image is the module pullback $L_B$, without an additional scalar extension. It is exact. The flat diagram-restriction lemma supplies $L_B\dashv F_B$ and the termwise adjunction. Exactness for towers is levelwise, so $L_B^J$ is exact. The exact-left-adjoint K-injective criterion now makes $F_B$ and $F_B^J$ preserve K-injectives. The same criterion makes ordinary inverse limit preserve K-injective tower complexes: the constant-tower functor $\Delta_T$ is exact by the levelwise criterion and is left adjoint to $\lim$, since a map $\Delta_T M\to C$ is exactly a compatible family $M\to C_n$. Therefore, for a K-injective $S_U$-tower complex $I$, all of $r_UI$, $F_S^JI$, $F_R^Jr_UI$, $\lim I$, $\lim r_UI$ and their direct images needed below are K-injective. Restrictions of these K-injectives are K-injective by step 1. No exactness of products was used.

For any strict tower complex $C$, right-adjoint preservation of limits gives $\beta_C^B:F_B\lim_{B_U}C\cong\lim_{B_V}F_B^JC$, characterized by projection $n$ equal to $F_B(p_n)$. The following ordinary identity holds:
$$\lim_{R_V}(\delta_C)\,\rho_{V,F_S^JC}\,r_V(\beta_C^S)
=\beta_{r_UC}^R\,F_R(\rho_{U,C})\,\delta_{\lim_{S_U}C}.$$
Indeed the $n$th projection of the left side is $\delta_{C_n}\,r_V(F_S(p_n))$. The $n$th projection of the right side is $F_R(r_U(p_n))\,\delta_{\lim_{S_U}C}$. These are equal by naturality of the ordinary scalar/direct-image comparison $\delta$ with respect to $p_n$. Projections determine a map into the ordinary limit, giving the equality degreewise; it is an equality of chain maps since all comparisons commute with differentials. This argument uses projections in the module category, not a purported universal property of a homotopy limit in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A07, ordinary tower-topos square

proof.text:
We spell out the normalization of $\kappa$ on the common model. For K-injective $I$, write $h^B_A:QF_BA\to R_u^B(QA)$ and $g^B_I:QF_B^JI\to\mathscr R_u^B(QI)$ for the universal units. Set
$$A_I^B=R_u^B(e^B_{U,I})\,h^B_{\lim I},\qquad
B_I^B=\mathcal L_V^B(g^B_I)\,e^B_{V,F_B^JI}.$$
All these maps are isomorphisms by steps 2 and 4. The direct-image/limit lemma specifies the comparison induced by the common ordinary composite; thus its composite-derived units give
$$\kappa_u^B(QI)\,A_I^B=B_I^B\,Q(\beta_I^B).$$
This also holds with $B=R$ and $I$ replaced by $r_UI$. The prescribed scalar comparisons similarly satisfy
$$d_{u,QI}\,r_V(g^S_I)=g^R_{r_UI}\,Q(\delta_I),\qquad
\chi_{u,QA}\,r_V(h^S_A)=h^R_{r_UA}\,Q(\delta_A)$$
for every K-injective $A$, by their normalization in the flat diagram-restriction statement. These are formulas for the specified maps, with their universal units retained.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), common composite; derived.tex Tags 070Y and 070K, units on K-injectives

proof.text:
Evaluate the desired equality at $QI$ and precompose both sides with the isomorphism $r_V(A_I^S)$ of step 6. Substitute the three unit-normalization equations of steps 3 and 6. Naturality moves $d$ across $g$, $\lambda$ across $g$, and $\chi$ across $e$. In detail, the left composite becomes
$$B_{r_UI}^R\,Q\bigl(\lim_{R_V}(\delta_I)\,\rho_{V,F_S^JI}\,r_V(\beta_I^S)\bigr),$$
whereas the right composite becomes
$$B_{r_UI}^R\,Q\bigl(\beta_{r_UI}^R\,F_R(\rho_{U,I})\,\delta_{\lim_{S_U}I}\bigr).$$
The maps inside $Q$ are exactly the two sides of step 5. They agree, so the displayed composites agree. Cancel $r_V(A_I^S)$ to obtain exactly the requested derived square. This computation cancels specified unit isomorphisms only; it does not choose a replacement comparison with the same endpoints.

source.place: Second paragraph, conjugation by direct-image/limit isomorphisms; explicit scalar unit calculation

proof.text: The constructed $\lambda$ is natural by step 3; $\kappa$, $d$ and $\chi$ are natural by their cited statements. For arbitrary $Z$, choose an isomorphism $v:Z\to QI$ as in step 2. If $P_Z,Q_Z$ denote the two composites in the claimed equation, their naturality gives $T(v)P_Z=P_{QI}S(v)$ and $T(v)Q_Z=Q_{QI}S(v)$, where $S=r_VR_u^S\mathcal L_U^S$ and $T=\mathcal L_V^R\mathscr R_u^Rr_U$. Step 7 gives $P_{QI}=Q_{QI}$, and $T(v)$ is invertible, hence $P_Z=Q_Z$. This proves the assertion for every derived strict-tower object, with naturality for every derived morphism, not only strict maps between selected resolutions. The argument uses neither finite coefficient reduction nor completeness.
